newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Holzmann groups discuss share pooling.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Holzmann groups discuss share pooling.

text.p: The two major shareholders of Germany's largest construction group, Philipp Holzmann AG, confirmed on Monday they were in talks over a possible plan to pool their stakes.

Such an arrangement, involving a 25.8 percent stake held by Deutsche Bank AG and a 20 percent interest held by construction group Hochtief AG, would be aimed at increasing Hochtief's management control over Holzmann.
The proposed deal would also seek to sidestep resistance shown by German cartel authorities in Hochtief's two-and-a-half-year campaign to increase the size of its direct stake in Holzmann.

A spokesman for Deutsche confirmed on Monday that it was in talks over such a plan but that no deal had been reached. A spokeswoman for Hochtief, the country's second largest builder, later also confirmed that talks were taking place.
Shares in Holzmann surged 29 marks, more than five percent, to 549 marks on speculation that a deal was imminent, although construction analysts noted that trading volumes were low.

This weekend, the Sueddeutsche Zeitung regional newspaper reported that a decision on the pooling together of shares could be made this week at a Deutsche supervisory board meeting, whose agenda is not known.

Separately, a German court of appeals is due next month to start hearings as to whether Hochtief should be allowed to extend its stake further by approving the purchase of one block of 4.9 percent and allowing it to take up options on a further 10 percent.
The Federal Cartel Office, Germany's main competition authority, has earlier blocked such moves, citing fears that the two would dominate the domestic market.
Construction analysts said they saw the share pooling plan as a "safety net" arrangement if the appeal court left the orginal decision by the cartel authority intact.
"But I don't immediately see what purpose this could serve for Hochtief," Karin Brinkmann, analyst at Munich-based Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel-Bank said.

Other analysts also noted that because of the size of the two companies -- Hochtief is the second largest in the sector -- the cartel authorities would also look critically at any colloboration between the two groups that was achieved through any pooling deal.
European Commission competition authorities might also need to approve the deal, they added.
